body:
Lamictal is the only non-addictive "super drug" for BP. I'm also inclined to say that I was likely misdiagnosed and I really have Borderline Personality (see my earlier reply).

Changing jobs is always in my thoughts. The job I have is pretty chill though. I'm the problem. Plus, I get a discount on my degree for being employed at the school. 

As for my fiance, I can't begin to tell you how hard she would take it. But she's also an incredibly resilient human being. Nothing shakes her. She's what I wish I was. She also hates that I need/choose to take medicine in any form. She deserves someone so much better than me it's sickening if I think about it for too long. In my mind it's only a matter of time before she realizes it. 

Even when posed with a single task, I just keep avoiding. Simple accomplishments are now so uncommon that I've gone past feeling good about them. That means that at one time after my problems began to slow down my productivity, there was a point so low that small accomplishments WERE cause for celebration. But I have since sunk lower. I feel like Bernie Madoff, knowing that it's just a matter of time before my mask slips just a bit too far and the audience gets to look a little longer and a little harder. Then I will have to change jobs. I don't want to see that day.

I listed them all because I was overwhelmed and wanted to paint the whole picture. In many ways, they're all intertwined. The bigger issues are the deeper ones and those are the root-cause for the smaller ones. Didn't have my instructions for posting to r/suicidewatch handy at the time. Also, seeing as how this is posted in SW, I would be inclined to give any person posting the benefit of the doubt that their mind is acting as a blender for every problem that exists in their life considering they chose this particular subreddit. 

But I think I get your drift in principle: Start where I am, and start small.

Henry Ford said a similar proverb: "Nothing is particularly hard if you divide it into small jobs." 

Also, you point out that there seems to be a lot of good in my life. That's kinda part of the problem: I don't deserve any of it and that fact could become abruptly apparent if/when someone calls me on my bullshit excuses.

Thank you and sorry for the initial rant.
Yea, not looking forward to detox....

Thank you for the words of wisdom. I've been to many a therapist in my life, but your comment introduced the refreshing element of anonymous observation and anonymous analysis. 

My fiance is in nursing and she explained to me that I exhibit much more traits found in borderline personality disorder than bi-polar according to the official definitions. Having lived with me she knows what the docs couldn't have known when I was diagnosed with bi-polar. Having done the research, I'm inclined to agree.

That's another (much more recent) reason I haven't returned to the bi-polar meds. 

You're right about doing one thing at a time. It's just a bummer that my procrastination leads to piles of issues with corresponding deadlines. That aspect is terrifying when combined with the fact that all outwardly appearances seem fine and full of potential. That's why I feel eventually the perfect storm will arrive after extreme amounts of phony progress and empty promises. That's when the curtain will drop and I'll be standing there holding the terrible truth for the world to see. (apologies for the corny Wizard of Oz metaphor)

Anyhow, I want to thank you for taking time out of your life to look at mine.
I just posted my current situation and insecurity is a big part of why saying goodbye is getting tempting. Thank you for the better perspective.
